paragraphs: Efficient attention mechanisms reduce the computational burden of full attention, but efficiency alone does not establish whether they can perform the same computations. This paper studies that question theoretically, focusing on sequential function composition: a reasoning task in which several dependent operations must be completed within a single forward pass.

The authors establish a separation based on network depth and attention type. A full-attention network with L+1 layers is sufficient for the task. By contrast, a hybrid network containing L−1 full-attention layers cannot solve it even when those layers are interleaved with 2^(3L²) linear-attention layers. The analysis covers linear-attention variants expressible as recurrences, including Mamba and DeltaNet.

The significance is that an enormous increase in recurrent linear-attention depth cannot compensate for the specified reduction in full-attention layers on this task. This provides a rigorous expressiveness hierarchy for the studied computation. Its scope is a theoretical separation on sequential composition, rather than a claim that full attention performs better on every practical language-model task.
icml-2026-a-provable-expressiveness-hier.tldr: A theoretical separation shows that vastly more linear-attention layers cannot replace a small number of full-attention layers for a particular multi-step reasoning task.

paragraphs: When a model learns new classes over time, the representations of previously learned classes can change. Nearest Class Mean classification summarizes each class with one representative point and is valued for resisting forgetting. Its theoretical justification assumes that examples from a class collapse toward a single point, an ideal that incomplete training and nonlinear representation changes can prevent.

HC-SOINN instead represents the more complex shape occupied by each class. It builds a hierarchy from local structure to a global description, allowing classification to account for class geometry beyond an average. The accompanying STAR method tracks individual points as their representations move and uses those trajectories to reshape the learned structure as the model changes.

The authors support resistance to these deformations with theoretical analysis and experiments using Procrustes distance. Replacing the classifiers in seven existing state-of-the-art methods produced consistent improvements. The findings support preserving and updating class structure when the single-point approximation is inadequate, while demonstrating that the classifier can improve multiple existing incremental-learning approaches.
icml-2026-beyond-point-wise-neural-colla.tldr: HC-SOINN improves class-incremental learning by representing class geometry and adapting that structure as learned features drift.

paragraphs: An uncertain prediction can reflect noise in the data or uncertainty in the model itself. The paper distinguishes these as aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. Networks that estimate a mean and variance can capture data noise, but may overfit and require additional regularization. Bayesian neural networks address model uncertainty, although approximate Bayesian inference makes them difficult to train.

The proposed method trains a variance-estimation network cooperatively with a Bayesian neural network. This brings the two uncertainty estimates into a shared training approach. The authors empirically find that the resulting model separates the two sources of uncertainty while also improving its estimate of the mean prediction.

Evaluation covers diverse datasets, including a newly created regression dataset whose noise varies over time and whose aleatoric uncertainty is known. That known uncertainty provides a direct reference for evaluating the noise estimate. The reported results support the method's effectiveness and scalability, and the authors describe it as robust, straightforward to implement, and compatible with different model architectures.
icml-2026-cooperative-variance-estimatio.tldr: Cooperatively training variance estimation and Bayesian networks empirically separates data noise from model uncertainty while improving mean predictions.

paragraphs: Autoregressive video diffusion can generate frames as a stream, but visual mistakes can accumulate as generation continues. Image quality and motion may deteriorate when the model produces videos much longer than those used in training. Deep Forcing addresses this problem by changing how the model retains and uses context, without additional training.

Its Deep Sink mechanism reserves approximately half of the sliding context window for persistent tokens. It adjusts their temporal positional phases to the current timeline so that this older context remains usable during extended generation. Participative Compression manages the stored attention information by retaining tokens that contribute to recent attention and pruning redundant or degraded history.

Together, these mechanisms support more than twelvefold length extrapolation, including extending a model trained on five-second videos to over sixty seconds. The authors report improved visual fidelity and motion without sacrificing inference speed. They also report performance comparable to leading methods trained specifically for long videos, suggesting that context preservation and selective removal can substantially improve long-duration generation.
icml-2026-deep-forcing-training-free-lon.tldr: Deep Forcing extends video generation without retraining by preserving useful global context and pruning attention history that no longer helps.

paragraphs: Global backpropagation couples parameter updates across a network's layers: updates depend on gradients propagated through the network. This dependency creates the update-locking problem. Depth-progressive Monotonic Learning, or DMoL, introduces local objectives for individual layers and progressively refines them across depth, allowing parameter updates without that global dependency.

The approach also permits network depth to change during training. The authors present this as a way to adapt to available computation and device resources while maintaining stable optimization. Their theoretical guarantees concern the local belief objectives: these improve monotonically as depth increases and converge exponentially. These guarantees describe the objectives themselves, rather than asserting that every additional layer must improve test accuracy.

Across the evaluated tasks, DMoL consistently matches or exceeds backpropagation. Reported results include a 4.3% accuracy gain on CIFAR-100, a 37.5% improvement on Cora alongside reduced over-smoothing in deep graph networks, and over 35% lower final loss in diffusion training. These findings support local training as a flexible alternative across several network applications.
icml-2026-depth-progressive-monotonic-le.tldr: DMoL uses progressively refined local layer objectives to unlock parameter updates and support changing network depth during training.

paragraphs: Many image generators first compress images into latent representations and then learn to generate within that space. The distribution of those representations affects the modeling problem. This paper asks how deliberately shaping that distribution can help retain image information while making the latent space easier for a generative model to learn.

Distribution-Matching VAE introduces a constraint that aligns the encoder's latent distribution with a chosen reference distribution. The reference need not be the Gaussian prior associated with conventional VAEs. It can instead come from self-supervised features, diffusion noise, or other priors, providing a framework for comparing different distribution structures within the same general approach.

The authors find that distributions derived from self-supervised learning offer a strong balance between reconstruction fidelity and modeling efficiency. They report a generation FID of 3.2 on ImageNet after 64 training epochs. The broader finding is that distribution-level alignment provides a useful design choice: the structure of the latent distribution can help reconcile faithful image reconstruction with efficient generative modeling.
icml-2026-distribution-matching-variatio.tldr: DMVAE explicitly matches image latents to chosen reference distributions, finding that self-supervised feature distributions balance reconstruction and generation efficiency.

paragraphs: Adapting a large pretrained diffusion model requires deciding how its parameters should change for a new task. FeRA approaches this through the model's behavior during denoising. The authors investigate how reconstruction progresses across frequency bands and propose aligning adaptation with that changing distribution of frequency energy.

The framework has three cooperating parts. A compact indicator summarizes how energy is distributed across bands in the latent representation. A soft router uses that information to combine multiple adapters specialized for different frequencies. A consistency regularizer encourages coherent adaptation across bands and stabilizes optimization, connecting the adapter updates to the same frequency-based description.

Routing remains active during inference, when the current latent's frequency energy determines the mixture of adapters. Thus, the adaptation mechanism responds to the representation being denoised rather than using one fixed mixture throughout generation. The authors report compatibility with adapter-based tuning and generalization across diffusion backbones and resolutions, presenting frequency-aware routing as a stable and broadly compatible approach to diffusion adaptation.
icml-2026-fera-frequency-energy-constrai.tldr: FeRA adapts diffusion models by routing among frequency-specific adapters according to the latent representation's changing energy distribution.

paragraphs: Sinkhorn iterations are widely used to solve entropic optimal transport problems, but their GPU implementations can spend substantial effort moving data. Dense implementations incur quadratic traffic to high-bandwidth memory. Existing online methods avoid storing the full interaction matrix, yet their generic reduction kernels still leave opportunities to combine operations and reduce memory transfers.

FlashSinkhorn targets squared Euclidean transport costs. It rewrites numerically stabilized Sinkhorn updates as row-wise LogSumExp reductions over biased dot products, exposing the same normalization structure used in transformer attention. Fused Triton kernels then stream tiles through on-chip memory and update the dual potentials in a single pass, reducing external memory traffic while keeping memory requirements linear.

Additional streaming kernels apply the transport operation and support first- and second-order optimization. On A100 GPUs, the authors report speedups of up to 32 times for forward passes and 161 times end to end against leading online baselines on point-cloud transport. The results demonstrate the practical value of organizing transport computation around GPU data movement, with improved scalability on downstream transport-based tasks.
icml-2026-flashsinkhorn-io-aware-entropi.tldr: FlashSinkhorn reorganizes squared-Euclidean optimal transport into fused GPU operations that sharply reduce memory traffic and accelerate computation.

paragraphs: Instruction-tuning datasets can mix examples from different domains and with different reasoning demands. Randomly shuffling them is a strong baseline, but it can place conflicting training objectives next to one another. EP-Order investigates whether ordering related examples together can make optimization more effective by accounting for relationships within the dataset.

The method first trains a warm-up model on a small subset, such as ten percent of the data. It uses that model to embed all training examples, groups them into clusters, and orders those clusters by embedding proximity. Unlike approaches that score examples individually, the ordering depends on how examples relate to one another in representation space.

Abrupt transitions between clusters can create sharp gradient changes and forgetting. EP-Order therefore inserts mixed regions containing examples from the previous, current, and next clusters. Across fourteen benchmarks covering vision-language, text-only, and hybrid thinking settings, it delivers broadly consistent improvements over random shuffling. The findings suggest that both grouping related data and smoothing transitions between groups can improve instruction tuning.
icml-2026-group-wise-data-ordering-enhan.tldr: EP-Order improves instruction tuning by arranging related training examples into nearby groups and blending examples at group transitions.

paragraphs: CLIP can generalize without task-specific training, but adapting it to a substantially different domain with only a few labeled examples remains difficult. This paper examines the common practice of aligning every image patch token with its corresponding text representation. It finds that this uniform treatment can be counterproductive for some tokens.

The authors call low-similarity image tokens tail tokens and observe that pushing them away from the text embedding consistently improves target-domain performance. Their interpretation is conditional on large domain shifts and scarce data: some visual tokens lack sufficient semantic information, so forcing them into alignment can encourage excessive fitting to the few available examples.

Adaptive Tail-Head Alignment turns this observation into a fine-tuning strategy that can strengthen or weaken alignment as appropriate. It replaces a uniform objective with selective treatment of image tokens. Experiments on four challenging cross-domain few-shot benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance. The findings support adapting alignment to the information already present in a token, especially when limited target data makes indiscriminate alignment unreliable.
icml-2026-improving-clip-adaptation-by-b.tldr: ATHA improves few-shot CLIP adaptation by selectively strengthening useful image-text alignment and weakening alignment for low-similarity tokens.

paragraphs: The paper investigates whether phase can carry useful information for neural sequence modeling independently of activation magnitude. Standard transformer representations can entangle the importance of a feature with its size. PRISM creates a constrained setting for studying an alternative by using complex-valued representations whose magnitude is fixed at one.

Within this setting, PRISM replaces attention with gated harmonic convolutions. The design encourages the model to suppress noise through subtractive interference in the frequency domain. The authors also study a hybrid architecture that combines phase-based routing with standard attention, reporting improved parameter efficiency and representation quality relative to baselines in their evaluated settings.

Interventions provide evidence about the mechanism: preserving phase largely preserves performance, whereas disrupting phase causes severe degradation. This supports the interpretation that substantial task-relevant information resides in phase. The conclusion is appropriately specific: spectral interference is a usable computational mechanism at the evaluated scale. The experiments support that modeling approach without establishing that language itself is universally governed by wave dynamics.
icml-2026-language-as-a-wave-phenomenon-.tldr: PRISM provides experimental evidence that phase-based interference can carry task-relevant information and improve sequence modeling in the evaluated settings.

paragraphs: Chemical language models often express intermediate reasoning as a written chain of thought. LatentChem investigates whether requiring this verbal form constrains chemical reasoning that could instead proceed internally. Its reasoning interface separates chemical computation from language generation, allowing the model to use continuous thought vectors together with dynamic perception.

A central observation is spontaneous internalization under optimization based only on task outcomes. The model increasingly chooses implicit latent computation over lengthy written derivations without being directly rewarded for that choice. The authors interpret this behavior as evidence that continuous representations provide a useful substrate for the chemical reasoning tasks they study.

On ChemCoTBench, LatentChem achieves a 59.88% win rate against a strong chain-of-thought baseline when ties are excluded. Across all evaluated benchmarks, it reduces reasoning-step overhead by an average factor of 10.84 and delivers a 5.96-fold wall-clock speedup. These findings connect the change in reasoning interface to both task performance and computational efficiency, providing empirical support for latent chemical reasoning in the evaluated settings.
icml-2026-latentchem-from-textual-cot-to.tldr: LatentChem lets chemical reasoning proceed through continuous internal representations, improving benchmark outcomes while substantially reducing reasoning time.

paragraphs: CLIP's strong zero-shot classification can coexist with reliance on misleading associations. A model may connect a target label with background or gender-related information that does not reliably identify the target. Locate-Then-Correct examines this problem at the level of attention heads inside the vision transformer, seeking specific internal contributors to those associations.

The method uses a contrastive framework to identify heads associated with spurious information and suppresses their influence through targeted ablation. It also identifies heads that carry salient information for the task. An orthogonal projection step incorporates discriminative features from those useful heads to improve classification, combining removal of misleading signals with use of relevant ones.

On benchmarks containing background and gender biases, the authors report more than a 50% gain in worst-group accuracy compared with non-training post-hoc baselines. They also visualize representations from selected heads and find support for the proposed identification mechanism. The results suggest that distinguishing useful and spurious heads can improve performance for the groups most poorly served by biased classification.
icml-2026-locate-then-correct-debiasing-.tldr: Locate-Then-Correct identifies and suppresses spurious CLIP attention heads while incorporating task-relevant features to improve worst-group classification.

paragraphs: Learning hidden dynamics from high-dimensional time series requires recovering a latent state and understanding how it evolves. Earlier identifiability results largely study the state while conditioning on predefined environment labels. This leaves questions about recovering the environment and dynamics function themselves, and about handling environments that were not assigned labels during training.

Meta-iLaD works with locally stationary latent dynamics governed by past latent states and an environment variable. It replaces label-based conditioning with a conditional prior implemented by a feedforward meta-learner. That learner extracts the environment variable from a few examples, giving the model a way to adapt its description of the dynamics from observations.

The authors establish simultaneous identifiability of the latent state, environment variable, and dynamics function within their formulation, without restricting the environment variable's dimension or how it modulates the dynamics. Empirical results support generalization to out-of-distribution environments using few-shot conditioning. They also indicate that identifying the environment and dynamics matters for forecasting, beyond successfully reconstructing trajectories already observed.
icml-2026-meta-ilad-identifiable-latent-.tldr: Meta-iLaD learns environment information from a few examples and establishes joint identifiability of latent states, environments, and their dynamics.

paragraphs: Feature learning strength controls an important aspect of how neural-network representations evolve during optimization. The paper defines it through the inverse of effective output scaling and asks how it affects generalization under a practical stopping rule: ending training once a target training risk is reached. This differs from studying only extreme strengths or indefinitely long training.

Empirical studies in deep networks reveal an intermediate strength that generalizes better than settings that are either too weak or too strong. This challenges the intuition that increasing feature learning must always help. The result motivates an explanation of why two models reaching a training target can nevertheless differ in performance beyond their training data.

The theoretical analysis studies gradient flow in two-layer ReLU networks trained with logistic loss, controlling feature learning strength through initialization scale. It establishes an optimum arising from competing effects: excessive strength causes over-alignment, while insufficient strength causes over-fitting. The contribution links the empirical pattern to a specific theoretical setting and makes feature learning strength a meaningful quantity to balance.
icml-2026-over-alignment-vs-over-fitting.tldr: The paper finds and theoretically explains an intermediate feature learning strength that balances over-alignment against over-fitting.

paragraphs: Generating an explorable 360-degree scene requires visual content to remain coherent as the viewpoint moves. PanoWorld-X addresses geometric inconsistencies that arise when video generation treats the scene mainly as changing two-dimensional pixels. Its approach uses panoramic representations and three-dimensional motion signals to better connect generation with the geometry of the surrounding environment.

The framework includes a data-curation pipeline for scene sequences with substantial movement and associated trajectories. Exploration Panoramic Plücker Embedding supplies guidance tailored to three-dimensional motion. A sphere-aware attention mechanism then reprojects features onto a sphere, allowing attention to reflect geometric adjacency in the panorama rather than relying solely on positions in a flat image.

These components address complementary requirements: examples of scene evolution, precise movement control, and spatial relationships suited to panoramic content. The authors report superior motion range, control precision, and visual quality in extensive experiments. The findings support the potential of spherical geometry and motion-aware guidance for immersive scene generation, while the stated results concern generated visual worlds rather than a guarantee of complete physical simulation.
icml-2026-panoworld-x-generating-explora.tldr: PanoWorld-X combines panoramic geometry, sphere-aware attention, and 3D motion guidance to generate more controllable explorable visual scenes.

paragraphs: Answering an image-based question may require outside knowledge, but retrieved material can conflict with other evidence. REAL addresses both recognizing those conflicts and controlling how they affect the answer. Its organizing concept is a reasoning-pivot: a small unit in a reasoning chain where a knowledge connection typically depends on external evidence.

A pivot can be a node or an edge in the chain. This focuses attention on the particular connection that needs support, rather than treating every reasoning step alike. Using the constructed REAL-VQA dataset, the authors train a discriminator through Reasoning-Pivot Aware supervised fine-tuning, connecting conflict identification with extraction of these evidence-dependent units.

During answer generation, Reasoning-Pivot Guided Decoding uses the pivots to target conflicting information within the model's own decoding process. Experiments across diverse datasets report significantly improved discrimination accuracy and superior overall performance. The findings support connecting conflict detection to the precise knowledge links used in reasoning, so that detecting a disagreement can directly inform how the answer is generated.
icml-2026-real-resolving-knowledge-confl.tldr: REAL detects and mitigates conflicting evidence by identifying the specific knowledge links that visual-question reasoning depends on.

paragraphs: Relational deep learning represents a database as a graph of different entity and relationship types, then uses a graph neural network for prediction. When some classes are much less common, their information can be overwhelmed by majority-class entities. Rel-MOSS addresses this imbalance in database entity classification by explicitly using the structure of relationships.

First, a relation-wise gating controller adjusts the neighborhood messages associated with each relation type. This helps prevent minority-related information from being submerged during representation learning. A second component generates synthetic minority examples using those gated representations and the entities' relational signatures, with the aim of preserving consistency with the database's relationship structure.

The two components connect representation learning and oversampling: the method changes both how relational information is gathered and how minority examples are supplemented. Across twelve entity-classification datasets, the authors report average improvements of up to 2.46% in Balanced Accuracy and 4.00% in G-Mean against leading relational-learning and conventional imbalance-handling methods. These results support treating relationships as part of the imbalance problem itself.
icml-2026-rel-moss-towards-imbalanced-re.tldr: Rel-MOSS improves imbalanced database classification through relation-specific message control and relationally consistent synthetic minority examples.

paragraphs: Spiking neural networks process information over timesteps, so allowing more steps might be expected to enrich their temporal computation. The authors observe a contrary pattern: increasing timesteps can reduce accuracy. They connect this timestep scaling paradox to gradients fading across long temporal spans and to weakened dependencies between different timesteps.

Their Timestep-Scalable neuron model introduces long-term memory reconsolidation to strengthen information flow across time. It pairs this with a temporal forgetting mechanism that periodically truncates the accumulation path. These mechanisms address different needs: retaining useful long-range information while preventing excessive temporal buildup from destabilizing training.

Theoretical analysis and extensive experiments support the design. In the reported evaluations, the model consistently improves as timesteps increase, achieves state-of-the-art results on time-series and event-based tasks, and remains strong on static-image classification and object detection. The findings suggest that extra timesteps become useful when the neuron model supports learning across them and controls accumulation, rather than merely extending the duration of computation.
icml-2026-resolving-the-timestep-scaling.tldr: The TS neuron combines long-term information flow with controlled forgetting to make additional timesteps beneficial in the reported spiking-network evaluations.

paragraphs: A successful jailbreak does not necessarily erase a language model's internal safety-related signals. This paper presents evidence that attacks selectively suppress some attention heads while others remain active. It distinguishes early-layer Adversarially Compromised Heads from middle-layer Safety-Aligned Heads, which retain robust activations even when the model produces a response that bypasses refusal.

Ablation experiments support different functional roles for these groups. Suppressing a small number of compromised heads is sufficient to produce jailbreak-like behavior on inputs the model would normally refuse. Removing safety-aligned heads substantially weakens the persistent middle-layer safety activations. Token-level attribution links suppression of the compromised heads specifically to tokens in the attack template.

Together, these observations explain how refusal behavior can fail while internal safety signals survive, a phenomenon the authors call Robust Harmful Features. Reading those persistent activations without training yields competitive aggregate detection performance and strong adversarial robustness. The practical implication is that internal signals can remain useful for detecting harmful inputs even after an attack has disrupted the model's outward refusal decision.
icml-2026-robust-harmful-features-under-.tldr: The paper finds that jailbreaks can suppress refusal-related attention heads while leaving persistent internal safety signals useful for detection.

paragraphs: Multimodal attacks can spread malicious intent across text and images, making each component less revealing when inspected alone. FlowGuard instead examines how a model combines the modalities internally. Its starting observation is that benign text-only and vision-only predictions tend to remain compatible when fused, while adversarial manipulation can disrupt that relationship.

The framework constructs FlowVectors inspired by Partial Information Decomposition. These describe cross-modal redundancy, synergy, and the dominance of information specific to one modality. By comparing unimodal and fused output distributions, they capture several aspects of the fusion process rather than reducing detection to a single confidence value.

A one-class classifier is trained only on benign examples to recognize departures from normal consistency. On the evaluated unseen attacks, FlowGuard reduces attack success rates from above 90% to below 15%, with less than 3% utility loss and up to a sixfold latency reduction. These results support internal cross-modal consistency as an efficient detection signal that can generalize beyond attacks explicitly represented in training.
icml-2026-securing-multimodal-ai-through.tldr: FlowGuard detects multimodal attacks by measuring inconsistencies between text-only, image-only, and fused predictions using a detector trained on benign data.

paragraphs: A small language model may propose a useful next token without ranking it first. Select to Think builds on this observation at points where small- and large-model reasoning diverges. The authors call it local sufficiency: the larger model's preferred token often already appears among the smaller model's highest-ranked candidates.

This changes the supervision problem. Instead of asking the small model to imitate the larger model's full generative distribution, S2T uses the larger model to rank a limited set of proposals. S2T-Local then distills this selection behavior into the small model, allowing it to rerank its own candidates without consulting the larger model during inference.

In the reported comparison, a 1.5-billion-parameter model's top eight candidates contain a 32-billion-parameter model's choice 95% of the time. S2T-Local improves the smaller model's Math Avg. by 24.1% relative to greedy decoding and matches the efficacy of eight-path self-consistency while using one trajectory. The results suggest that better local selection can recover substantial reasoning performance from candidates the small model already generates.
icml-2026-select-to-think-unlocking-slm-.tldr: S2T-Local improves small-model reasoning by teaching it to rerank its own token candidates without a large model at inference time.

paragraphs: Collaborating learning agents can benefit from exchanging knowledge even when their local models differ. Existing heterogeneous federated-learning approaches often share parameters or intermediate representations, which can add overhead and expose sensitive information. SoHip explores a memory-centered form of collaboration in which agents exchange lightweight abstractions of their learned knowledge.

Each agent first derives individual short-term memory from local representations. A hippocampus-inspired mechanism consolidates this into individual long-term memory. The agent then combines its own long-term memory with collectively aggregated long-term memory to improve local prediction. Throughout this process, raw data and local models stay on the device.

The authors provide theoretical analyses of convergence and privacy-preservation properties. Experiments on two benchmark datasets against seven baselines report consistent improvements, with accuracy gains of up to 8.78%. These findings support memory sharing as a collaboration mechanism for heterogeneous agents. The contribution connects local learning and collective knowledge through a shared memory representation, while keeping the agents' underlying models and data local.
icml-2026-social-hippocampus-memory-lear.tldr: SoHip enables heterogeneous agents to collaborate through lightweight consolidated memories while keeping raw data and local models on-device.

paragraphs: Contrastive vision-language learning aims to place images and text in a shared representation space, yet the two modalities often occupy separate regions. This modality gap has an unclear relationship with downstream performance. The paper develops a theoretical framework for understanding the geometry of convergent optimal representations when contrastive training is optimized.

Within this framework, the authors prove that a modality gap emerges when image and text representations collapse into different subspaces. Although that separation prevents direct alignment of the full representations, their projections onto a shared subspace can still align. This distinguishes global separation from the quality of the common information represented by both modalities.

The analysis identifies shared-space alignment as a dominant factor in downstream performance, with a more limited role for the modality gap itself. Motivated by this result, Shared Space Alignment modifies pretraining to strengthen alignment in the common subspace without explicitly reducing the gap. Extensive experiments support both the theoretical account and the method, suggesting a more targeted objective for improving multimodal representations.
icml-2026-the-convergent-representation-.tldr: The paper links vision-language performance to alignment within a shared subspace and proposes improving that alignment without explicitly closing the modality gap.

paragraphs: An agent's memory improves future behavior only if it captures useful lessons from experience. That requires both extracting the right information and deciding how to update the memory bank. UMEM addresses the problem that optimizing memory management while leaving extraction fixed can accumulate details tied to individual cases instead of reusable knowledge.

The framework jointly optimizes a language model to perform extraction and management. Its Semantic Neighborhood Modeling groups semantically related queries and evaluates the marginal usefulness of memory across those neighborhoods. A neighborhood-level reward, optimized with GRPO, encourages memories whose benefits extend beyond the particular interaction from which they were extracted.

Across five benchmarks, the authors report significant improvements over highly competitive baselines, including gains of up to 11.49 points on multi-turn interactive tasks. Performance also maintains a stable improvement trend during continued evolution. The findings support coordinating what gets remembered with how memory is maintained, and judging memory through its usefulness to related queries rather than a single isolated instance.
icml-2026-umem-unified-memory-extraction.tldr: UMEM jointly learns memory extraction and management, rewarding memories that help groups of related queries rather than only individual cases.
